title: Comparison and functoriality of constructible topologies on algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention] with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], their sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], and point spaces with the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. A space is quasi-compact if every open cover of its point space has a finite subcover; a morphism is quasi-compact if its pullback along every affine scheme test has quasi-compact point space. A space is quasi-separated if its absolute diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is quasi-compact. For a scheme, the constructible topology is locally the topology generated by quasi-compact opens and their complements on affine open charts. For an algebraic space, define its constructible topology to be the final topology for its representable etale affine scheme charts. For quasi-separated spaces these topologies are independent of the choice of a surjective etale scheme presentation and equal the quotient topology of the constructible topology of any such presentation. Every morphism between quasi-separated spaces induces a continuous map for their constructible topologies. The constructible topology is finer than the Zariski topology. A subset $F\subseteq|X|$ of a quasi-separated space is Zariski closed if and only if it is closed in the constructible topology and stable under specialization, meaning $x\in F$ and $z\in\overline{\{x\}}$ imply $z\in F$.

source.place: Rydh Proposition (1.2)(i), Corollary (1.5), and Remark (1.8), printed pp.4--7. Author PDF https://davidrydh.se/papers/submersion20100305.pdf read online; local copy WANTED.

proof.text: On an affine scheme $A$, use [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs] and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-scheme-spectral]. Quasi-compact opens are retrocompact: their intersections with quasi-compact opens are quasi-compact by spectrality. Thus finite intersections of the patch subbasic opens and their complements are constructible, by [def-weil-constructible-subset]. Conversely every constructible set is patch clopen by [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-constructible-clopen-constructible-topology]. Consequently constructible subsets form a basis for the patch topology on $A$. The same subbasis argument shows every patch-closed subset of $A$ is an intersection of constructible subsets: write its complement as a union of these basis elements and take complements.

The affine topologies glue as in the statement. If $B\subset A$ is an affine open in an affine scheme, it is quasi-compact and hence retrocompact in $A$. It is constructible and patch open by step 1. A constructible subset of $B$ is constructible in $A$ by [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-in-retrocompact-open]; the basis hypothesis holds by spectrality of $A$. Conversely the intersection with $B$ of a constructible subset of $A$ is constructible in $B$ by [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-intersection-in-constructible]. By step 1 these two assertions say exactly that $B$ has its own patch topology as the induced topology and is patch open. For two affine opens in any scheme, cover their intersection by affine opens $B$ contained in both; the preceding argument makes the two topologies agree on each $B$, hence on the intersection. Thus testing patch openness on an affine open cover defines a topology independent of that cover, each affine chart is patch open with its stated topology, and every Zariski open is patch open (locally it is a union of quasi-compact affine opens).

source.place: Tags 09YJ (lemma-constructible-in-constructible), 09YI (lemma-intersect-constructible-with-constructible), and the paragraph preceding Tag 0901

proof.text: Every scheme morphism $g:T\to V$ is patch continuous. Cover $T$ by affine opens $A$ mapping into affine opens $B$ of $V$; these exist since a scheme morphism is continuous in the Zariski topology [def-pc-scheme]. For each constructible basic patch open $C\subset B$, [lem-pur-scheme-constructible-preimage] applied to $A\to B$ makes $g^{-1}(C)\cap A$ constructible in $A$, hence patch open by step 1. The affine charts are patch open by step 2, so these local continuity assertions give continuity on $T$. This does not assume $g$ quasi-compact.

Every etale scheme morphism $g:T\to V$ is patch open. Fix an affine open $B\subset V$ and cover $g^{-1}(B)$ by affine opens $A\subset T$. The restriction $g|_A:A\to B$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]: the open immersions $A\to T$ and $B\to V$ are etale by its clause (1), the composite $A\to T\to V$ is etale by clause (2), and since this composite equals $A\to B\to V$ with $B\to V$ etale, clause (3) makes $A\to B$ etale. It is locally of finite presentation by [def-weil-etale-morphism] and quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], since $A$ is quasi-compact and $B$ quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. If $H$ is patch open in $T$, write $H\cap A$ as a union of constructible subsets $C$ of $A$ using steps 1--2. For each $C$, [lem-weil-pbc-chevalley-constructible-image] gives $g(C)$ constructible in the qcqs affine $B$, hence patch open by step 1. Their union, over $C$ and $A$, is $g(H)\cap B$, proving the assertion by step 2. No quasi-compactness of $g$ or of $T$ is used.

source.place: Tag 054J (lemma-chevalley), using Tag 054I and affine localization; Rydh Proposition (1.2)(iii)

proof.text: For any scheme $T$, a patch-closed specialization-stable subset $E$ is Zariski closed. Indeed on each affine open $A$, $E\cap A$ is patch closed by step 2 and is an intersection of constructible subsets by step 1. The affine $A$ is spectral by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs] and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-scheme-spectral]. If $x\in\overline{E\cap A}$, [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-proconstructible-closure-specialization] produces $e\in E\cap A$ specializing to $x$ in $A$, hence in $T$. Specialization stability gives $x\in E\cap A$. Thus $E\cap A$ is closed in $A$, for every affine open $A$, so $E$ is closed in $T$. Conversely a Zariski closed subset is patch closed by step 2, and closed sets are stable under specialization by the definition of closure.

source.place: Tag 0903 (lemma-constructible-stable-specialization-closed), clauses (1)--(2), locally on affine charts

proof.text: Let $X$ be the algebraic space and fix any surjective etale scheme presentation $p:U\to X$, which exists by [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover]. Put the quotient of the patch topology of $U$ on $|X|$. For any etale scheme chart $t:T\to X$, [lem-a1-space-atlas-test-open-subsets] supplies the scheme $Q=T\times_XU$ with projections $q:Q\to T$ surjective etale and $b:Q\to U$ etale, and its stated inverse-image and image equalities. If $p^{-1}(H)$ is patch open, $b^{-1}(p^{-1}(H))$ is patch open by step 3; its image under $q$ is patch open by step 4 and equals $t^{-1}(H)$. Conversely if all affine etale charts have patch-open inverse image, apply this to the affine opens of $U$: their composites with $p$ are representable etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale] and [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]. Step 2 then gives $p^{-1}(H)$ patch open. Thus the quotient topology is exactly the final topology specified in the statement, for every presentation. This proves independence, including comparison with the local scheme topology when $X$ is a scheme (step 3 and the identity affine open charts).

source.place: Tag 03BX (lemma-topology-points), presentation-comparison proof; patch version uses Tags 054I and 054J as in steps 3--4

proof.text: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism and let $H\subseteq|Y|$ be patch open. Choose surjective etale scheme presentations $w:W\to X$ and $p:V\to Y$ by [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover]. Apply [lem-a1-space-atlas-test-open-subsets] to $t=f\circ w:W\to Y$ and $p$: it gives $Q=W\times_YV$, with $q:Q\to W$ surjective etale and $b:Q\to V$ a scheme morphism, and $q(b^{-1}(p^{-1}(H)))=w^{-1}(f^{-1}(H))$. The set $p^{-1}(H)$ is patch open by step 6, its inverse image under $b$ is patch open by step 3, and its image under $q$ is patch open by step 4. Step 6 for $w$ now gives $f^{-1}(H)$ patch open, as required. In particular no quasi-compactness of $f$, $W$, $V$, or the presentations is being presumed.

source.place: Tag 03BX (lemma-topology-points), morphism-continuity proof via presentations; scheme patch inputs from Tags 054I and 054J

proof.text: If $H\subseteq|X|$ is Zariski open, its inverse image under every affine etale chart is Zariski open by [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover], and hence patch open by step 2. By the final-topology definition $H$ is patch open. This proves the claimed fineness. A Zariski closed subset is therefore patch closed, and is stable under specialization because it contains the closure of each of its points.

source.place: Tag 03BX (lemma-topology-points), continuity of scheme-source maps; scheme fineness is the paragraph preceding Tag 0901

proof.text: Finally let $F\subseteq|X|$ be patch closed and stable under specialization. For every affine etale chart $t:A\to X$, $t^{-1}(F)$ is patch closed by step 6. It is specialization stable: the Zariski continuous point map $t$ from [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover] sends $z\in\overline{\{a\}}$ into $\overline{\{t(a)\}}$, since the inverse image of every closed subset containing $t(a)$ is closed and contains $a$. Thus step 5 says $t^{-1}(F)$ is Zariski closed. Its complement has open inverse image in every affine etale chart, hence in every etale scheme chart $T\to X$ by an affine open cover of $T$: each affine open $T_i\subseteq T$ gives an etale affine chart $T_i\to T\to X$, since $T_i\to T$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale] and the composite is representable etale by [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence] (for scheme sources chartwise etale equals representable etale, and composites are chartwise etale). The final atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology] says that $|X|\setminus F$ is Zariski open. This proves the other direction of the closedness criterion. These arguments apply in particular to every quasi-separated space in the statement.
